quiz_title: 🧠 AI Challenge 3: ML Image & Object Classifiers

questions.question: What is the Machine Learning Environment used for in PicToBlox?
options: To collect data samples, train custom ML models, and test them inside our scripts
questions.explanation: Correct! The ML Environment is our training suite to feed samples and generate custom neural models.

questions.question: What is the very first phase required to build a custom Image Classifier?
options: Collecting and labelling training image samples (data collection)
questions.explanation: Excellent! Data collection (loading photos and grouping them into labeled classes) is the core first phase of machine learning.

questions.question: Why do we feed the ML model multiple different photos of the same object (e.g. 50 photos of an elephant)?
options: To fill up hard drive space
To teach the model to recognize the object from different angles, distances, and lighting!
To speed up the camera transparency
questions.explanation: Perfect! Diverse image samples enhance training, teaching the model robust generalization patterns.

questions.question: Which block is used to load your custom-trained Image Classifier model into your PicToBlox project?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The 'load image classifier model' block fetches your trained weights into script memory.

questions.question: What block returns the prediction confidence percentage (how sure the computer is about its scan classification)?
questions.explanation: Great! The confidence rating (0 to 100%) indicates how certain the model is about its classification.

questions.question: How can we build a Mask Detector that warns people who aren't wearing medical masks?
options: Train a model with two classes: 'Mask' and 'No Mask', then check predictions in an if-else block!
questions.explanation: Perfect! Training a two-class binary image classifier and wrapping it in if-else statements solves this security check cleanly.

questions.question: What is Custom Object Detection in machine learning?
options: Counting how many faces are happy
Training a model to identify specific custom items (like your private pen or bottle) and locate their bounding boxes
questions.explanation: Spot on! Custom Object Detection localizes items on screen, drawing boundary coordinates around them.

questions.question: What does a bounding box represent in object detection scanners?
options: The rectangular coordinate boundary drawn around a detected item on the video feed
questions.explanation: Great! Bounding boxes show exactly where an item resides in the camera's coordinates grid.

questions.question: What happens after you finish training your custom ML model in the editor?
options: You export the model and can immediately interact with its custom prediction blocks in your scripts!
You must write code in C++
questions.explanation: Excellent! Once trained, custom blocks representing your classes become available in the ML drawer.

questions.question: Under which block drawer can you find your loaded machine learning blocks?
questions.explanation: Perfect! Pre-trained classification blocks live under the 'Machine Learning' extension drawer.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to load a trained image classifier model and identify the class of a live camera feed.
questions.task_hint: load image classifier model -> identify class from camera
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Loading the model and running real-time frame checks is the standard pipeline to classify feeds.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to check if the identified class is 'No Mask', and if so, play a warning beep sound.
questions.task_hint: if identified class == 'No Mask' then play sound 'warning_beep'
questions.explanation: Perfect! This simple script creates a highly useful automated safety checker!
